submitted.rationale: Index 120 (Fe 0.56, Ni 0.21, V 0.23) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 5.5e-7 A. The Fe-rich region beat the V-rich region, which fits a hematite-type absorber taking up 2.72 eV photons. A little V with Ni kept low improved on the most Fe-rich point.

rejected.reason: Most Fe-rich candidate; 4.8e-7 A, below index 120.
V-rich, FeVO4-like region; 2.1e-7 A, much lower.

consultations.verdict: Supportive, with low confidence. MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of about 2.77 eV for hematite (mp-19770). That is close to the 2.72 eV illumination, and HSE tends to overestimate the gap of Fe2O3 (the experimental gap is about 2.1 eV). So Fe-rich films with a hematite/FeVO4-type absorber should absorb at 455 nm. Index 145 has the highest Fe content in the library.

Somewhat supportive. MEGNet puts V2O5 (mp-25279) at a gap of about 2.8 eV HSE; the experimental value is about 2.3 eV. Fe-V mixtures near FeVO4 (gap about 2.0 eV) should absorb at 2.72 eV. Index 115 (Fe 0.32, Ni 0.18, V 0.50) is Fe:V-rich with little Ni, which tests the FeVO4-like region as a contrast to the Fe-rich point already measured.

Supportive. The hematite gap brackets (1.5 eV PBE, 2.77 eV HSE) fit visible absorption at 2.72 eV. The Fe-rich point (145) gave 4.8e-7 A, better than the V-rich point (115) at 2.1e-7 A. Index 120 is Fe-rich with a little more V and less Ni, which may improve charge transport; the GP also ranks it in its top 5.
